method: Differential whole-source review: all337 unified-diff lines inspected without truncation against fully reviewed Unix SSE2 assembly; remaining lines text-identical with SequenceMatcher autojunk disabled. No independent serial reread of identical lines.
findings: Hash-many adds RSI/RDI saves,528-byte stack reservation and XMM6..15 saves/restores at0x170..0x200. Incoming Windows registers are reshuffled and stacked counter/increment/flags/start/end/output are read at RBP+0x68/70/78/80/88/90 after eight pushes.

Both scalar functions reserve120 bytes and save XMM6,7,8,9,11,14,15. Windows-specific mask emulation uses XMM14 instead of Unix XMM10 for the upper-word blend temporary; this avoids modifying unsaved Windows-nonvolatile XMM10. This adaptation is present in both scalar functions.

Scalar pointers use RCX/RDX, length is zero-extended from R8b, flags from adjusted stack0xA0, counter R9. XOF output pointer from0xA8 goes to volatile R10; stores write64 bytes, in-place stores32 bytes. Restore sequences balance the frames.
Shared SSE2 rotations, mask constants, counter selection and groups4/2/1 remain text-identical except reviewed ABI changes. Constant section is .rdata and ELF/CET/Apple wrappers are removed.
No explicit unwind metadata directives observed. Balanced source saves and offsets do not establish Windows exception handling or runtime parity.
limits: No x86/Windows run, assembly build, sanitizer or throughput measurement; upstream reference-only, pHash/ASAN deferred.
